newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle seen steady next week-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle seen steady next week-trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets next week were seen unchanged at $68.00 per cwt amid expectations for moderate beef demand that could offset projections for slightly higher feedlot supplies, according to feedlot sources.
Feedlots this week were very current in their marketings, with only light numbers of cattle expected to be carried over onto showlists next week, they said.
Sales were brisk Tuesday at $68.00, down $2.00 from last week's top price. Packers bought early for next week's delivery because of the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday.

This week's declines were attributed to a bearish USDA monthly Cattle-On-Feed report last Friday, which showed larger than anticipated feedlot cattle supplies and aggressive placements of cattle during October.
Sales this week totalled 58,100 head in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and 72,100 in Kansas.
